messages:
maria.s: Heads-up — we had cross-region gRPC failures for service-ingest after the EU cert sweep at 09:10 UTC. Connections to eu-proxy started failing with TLS handshake errors.
jonathan.k: saw that. error in proxy logs is: `tls: handshake failure: tls: bad certificate`
ryan.ops: sec-bot flagged a KMS Decrypt error during container startup: `AccessDenied` for role `svc-ingest-eu` when trying to unwrap the TLS key.
maria.s: timeline: certs rotated (cert-manager) -> pods restarted -> failing handshakes + KMS decrypt denies. Seems like RBAC/role change coincided with rotation.
eva.p: I pulled audit logs. KMS shows Deny because the principal was `system:serviceaccount:ingest:default` — but the role binding changed yesterday in infra PR #3245 (purpose: tighten RBAC).
jonathan.k: can we confirm whether the cert-manager private key was encrypted with KMS key A vs key B? if certs were created using key A and we rotated KMS to key B without granting old principal access -> decrypt fails.
ryan.ops: command I ran:
```
aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/rlw-ingest-kms
kubectl -n ingest describe secret tls-ingest | grep "encrypted-"
```
returns grant id present but `aws kms test-iam-permissions` for svc-ingest-eu reports missing `kms:Decrypt`.
eva.p: remediation suggestion: add a short-lived grant for the service account to `kms:Decrypt` for key A, restart pods in EU region, confirm handshake, then tighten.
maria.s: agree. but we need incident notes for compliance: record who changed RBAC, when cert rotation started, and KMS audit entries.
sre-oncall: running canary restart in eu region now (rolling 10%): `kubectl -n ingest rollout restart deploy/ingest --max-surge=1 --max-unavailable=0`
sec-bot: [ALERT] KMS Decrypt Failure (svc-ingest-eu) 09:12 UTC — report id kb-20260318-001
jonathan.k: also worth checking TLS profile: some proxies had TLS1.2-only fallback disabled. If handshake error is cert/mac mismatch maybe due to SNI mismatch after new cert with altNames missing region label.
ryan.ops: quick check of cert subject altNames:
```
openssl x509 -in /etc/ingest/tls.crt -noout -text | grep -A1 "Subject Alternative Name"
```
one of the CNs had `eu.` prefix — looks like template bug in cert-manager clusterissuer for eu.
eva.p: proposed actions (short):
- emergency grant: add `kms:Decrypt` for svc-ingest-eu on key A (10m window)
- restart pods in eu (canary -> full) to pick up decrypted key
- patch cert-manager ClusterIssuer template to include region SNI
- revert RBAC PR or scope it properly
- collect and upload KMS & kube audit logs to secure storage for compliance
maria.s: who owns the RBAC PR? @jonathan.k or @ryan.ops? we need the reviewer to sign off on revert.
jonathan.k: PR authored by infra-team (me) but reviewer changed binding. I'll open PR to scope binding to `ingest-ci` instead of `default` SA and add an emergency revert.
sre-oncall: Can we add a fallback route to route traffic to us-west while eu is degraded? we should avoid plaintext fallback.
ryan.ops: routing fallback added: traffic will prefer us-west via smart-routing layer, forced TLS to us-west. Not ideal but keeps service online.
eva.p: follow-ups for postmortem/triage:
- add automated check: when rotating certs, validate KMS grants and SA mapping pre-rotation
- ensure clusterissuer templates are region-aware in CI tests
- extend KMS audit retention for 90d for compliance review
- add RBAC change notification in infra PRs (auto-tag sec-owners)
maria.s: thanks team. I'll create an incident ticket with required compliance artifacts and tag legal/compliance. Marking priority P2->P1 until certs stable.
jonathan.k: PR #3249 opened to revert RBAC reviewer change; will add a locked grant pattern and integration test.
eva.p: note: for TLS hardening config we should standardize on:
```
ssl_protocols TLSv1.3;
ssl_ciphers TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256:TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384;
ssl_prefer_server_ciphers on;
ssl_session_tickets off;
```
but test connectivity for older clients before force-enforcing.
maria.s: good. everyone drop incident evidence into the ticket. cc: sec-incident@redwood.com :thumbsup:
